correctness.rationale: Conditioning on a descent at position i turns the two adjacent values into the maximum and minimum of a uniformly chosen unordered pair. Their exact mean shifts are +(n+1)/6 and -(n+1)/6, while all other positions retain mean (n+1)/2. The weighted rank-sum shift is therefore exactly -(n+1)/6 independently of i, giving the local covariance after the affine conversion to squared displacement and Spearman's coefficient. Summation and standard exact permutation variances yield the global covariance and correlation. Exhaustive exact enumeration through n=9 and an independent conditional-pair replay through n=500 agree with every displayed formula.

value.rationale: Descents are the canonical local order-disagreement statistic, while Spearman's coefficient is a canonical global rank-displacement statistic. The theorem gives a structural local-to-global bridge: every adjacent position contributes exactly the same mean shift, and the total redundancy decays on a sharp n^{-1} scale. This directly quantifies how a local Eulerian summary and a global rank-correlation summary overlap under the permutation null.
